title: Modesty, Marriage, and the Light of Allah

paragraphs.text: There is no blame in entering empty buildings that are useful to you. Believing men should lower their gaze and guard their private parts. Believing women should do the same. They should not show their beauty except what normally appears. They should cover their chests with their head covers, except before close family and those listed in the verse. All believers should turn to Allah in repentance. Help the unmarried to marry, because Allah can make the poor rich. Those who cannot marry should stay chaste. Slaves who seek freedom should be given a contract and some wealth, and no one should force them into sin.

Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. His light is like a lamp in a niche. The lamp is inside glass that shines like a bright star. It is lit from a blessed olive tree whose oil almost glows by itself. Light upon light! Allah guides to His light whom He wills. In mosques, men praise Him morning and evening. Trade does not distract them from prayer and zakah.
The deeds of disbelievers are like a mirage that a thirsty man thinks is water. Or they are like layers of darkness in a deep sea, under waves and clouds. Whoever Allah gives no light has no light.
Everything in the heavens and earth praises Allah, even birds in flight. Allah drives the clouds, sends rain and hail, and changes night and day. He created every living creature from water.

hardWords.m: the way you look at things
a small hollow space in a wall
something seen in the desert that looks like water but is not
